Here is the full analysis:

---

## Restore Drill Post-Mortem: What Earned Its Place

### What Happened

The April drill recovered **4.1 GB** from the backup bucket. Configuration (~0.2 GB) was restored and services came up fine. Source code (~3.9 GB) was pulled, then immediately discarded — the tag in version control was three commits ahead, so the team rebuilt from the tag instead.

| Phase | Time | What happened |
|-------|------|---------------|
| Pull bucket | 09:10–09:40 | 4.1 GB downloaded |
| Config restore | 09:40 | Services start |
| Source check | 09:44 | Restored source is 3 commits behind tag |
| Source discarded | 09:50 | Rebuilt from tag instead |
| Drill complete | 10:05 | Only 25 minutes of actual work |

**And this wasn't a first-time mistake** — the report says source has been discarded in *all four* quarterly drills, because the backup copy is always older than the tag.

### Cost Breakdown

| Month | Total | Source | Config | Source share |
|-------|-------|--------|--------|-------------|
| Jan | 2.8 GB | 2.6 GB | 0.2 GB | 93% |
| Feb | 3.2 GB | 3.0 GB | 0.2 GB | 94% |
| Mar | 3.6 GB | 3.4 GB | 0.2 GB | 94% |
| Apr | 4.1 GB | 3.9 GB | 0.2 GB | 95% |

Config is flat at **0.2 GB** — tiny, stable, and always useful. Source is growing 0.4 GB/month and is never used. By April it made up **95% of the bucket**.

### Verdict

| Item | Size | Used in restore? | Earned its place? |
|------|------|------------------|-------------------|
| Configuration | 0.2 GB | ✅ Every drill | **Yes** — essential, small, can't be reconstructed |
| Source code | 3.9 GB | ❌ Never used | **No** — always stale, rebuilt from tag, growing fast |

### Root Cause

The backup is capturing the *wrong version* of source: whatever lived on the production server at backup time, which is always behind the tagged release in version control. Since the build is **reproducible from the tag** (CI/CD can reconstruct the exact artifact), the production source copy has no recoverable value.

### Recommendation: What a Project Backup Should Carry

**1. Configuration** — 0.2 GB, no change needed. This is the only thing that can't be reproduced from version control, and it's tiny.

**2. Remove source code from the backup entirely.** It adds ~4 GB and growing for zero recovery value. The team already proved in four consecutive drills that rebuilding from the tag is faster and more correct than restoring from backup.

**3. Optional addition — database dumps or user content**, if the project has any. Neither is mentioned in the current bucket, so this is just a gap check. If the project has mutable data that isn't in version control, *that* belongs in the backup alongside config.

**Bottom line:** A project backup should carry only what is **unique and unreproducible** — configuration (and any operational data). Reproducible artifacts built from tagged releases belong in version control and CI/CD, not in a backup bucket.

Agreed, and the drill made it obvious. Decision: src is regenerated from the build on every restore, so no backup carries src. It is the largest thing we store and the one thing we never read back. Recording it so the next drill does not re-derive it.
